Topographical maps are introduced by a brief historical account. Modern maps and plans are treated at some length, and include the latest Ordnance Survey work. Description of map-making is centred round the instruments involved, and includes a description and assessment of air survey, Projections are treated with a minimum of mathematics. Concluding chapters deal with map reading and the geographical interpretation of landscape as depicted on maps.

"A textbook based on Surveying, theory and practice."

The Department of Agricultural and Biological Engineering at Purdue University in West Lafayette, Indiana, presents information on surveying. This information is aimed at students in agricultural systems management courses. Topics covered include the history of surveying, measurement errors, rules of calculation, electronic distance measurement, leveling procedures and elevations, and more. Most of the information has been excerpted from the ninth edition of "Elementary Surveying," by Wolf and Brinker.

This book is intended for colleages and technical schools and is designed to facilitate self-study.The use of this equipment requires thorough understanding and much practice for success, while the use of more sophisticated equipment requires less understanding and less practice.Since the surveyor may be called on to to use any type of equipment, it seems advisable that he or she be well versed in the use of traditional equipment and have sufficient knowledge of basic principles to learn quickly the use of more modern equipment. This book is written in accordance with this philosophy.
